title: 2027 Bee Grant Program: Up to $2,000 and Educational Hive Support for Schools and Nonprofit Organizations
summary: The 2027 Bee Grant Program is now open for applications, providing schools and nonprofit organizations with an opportunity to establish, expand, or strengthen educational honey bee programs for students in grades K–12. The program is designed to bring pollinator education to life through hands-on experiences with live honey bee hives, classroom resources, curriculum materials, and other educational support. The Bee Grant is offered through The Bee Cause Project and Whole Kids , with support from the Whole Foods Market Foundation . It is intended to help educators create meaningful learning experiences that connect students with honey bees, pollinators, environmental conservation, science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics. For eligible schools and nonprofit organizations in the United States and Canada, the program can provide either a monetary grant or equipment support for developing an educational bee program. Previous Bee Grant recipients may also apply for the separate Renewal Bee Grant, which provides funding and additional program support for continuing and improving existing bee education initiatives. Applications for both the Traditional Bee Grant and Renewal Bee Grant open on September 1 and close on October 31 . What Is the 2027 Bee Grant Program? The Bee Grant Program is an educational initiative that helps schools and nonprofit organizations introduce students to the world of honey bees and pollinators. Rather than limiting bee education to textbooks or conventional classroom lessons, the program encourages hands-on learning through educational hive programs. Students can observe bees, learn about pollination, explore ecosystems, understand environmental stewardship, and develop practical knowledge about the role pollinators play in food systems and natural environments. Grant recipients can receive financial or equipment assistance to establish or improve their bee programs. In addition, educators gain access to curriculum materials, lesson plans, digital learning resources, and other tools designed to support the integration of pollinator education into the learning environment. The program is particularly relevant to schools and organizations interested in creating long-term environmental education programs rather than one-time classroom activities. Who Is Behind the Bee Grant? The program is brought to educators through The Bee Cause Project and Whole Kids , with support from the Whole Foods Market Foundation . The Bee Cause Project is dedicated to pollinator education and preservation and works to help students and educators understand the importance of bees and other pollinators. Through the Bee Grant, participating schools and organizations can create educational experiences that make pollinator science more accessible and practical for students. What Does the 2027 Bee Grant Provide? The support available through the program depends on whether an organization applies for the Traditional Bee Grant or Renewal Bee Grant. For new applicants, the Traditional Bee Grant offers two primary grant options: 1. Monetary Grant Eligible new applicants can apply for a $2,000 monetary grant to help build and support a live bee education program. The funding can help an institution develop the infrastructure and activities necessary to establish a meaningful educational bee program. 2. Equipment Grant Applicants may also choose an Equipment Grant , which includes: An indoor observation hive A $1,000 stipend An indoor observation hive provides students with an opportunity to observe honey bees and learn about hive activity in an educational setting. This type of equipment can serve as a long-term teaching resource, allowing educators to incorporate bee-related lessons into science, environmental studies, STEAM education, and other areas of the curriculum. Traditional Bee Grant for New Applicants The Traditional Bee Grant is specifically intended for new applicants. It is available to K–12 schools and nonprofit organizations serving students in grades K–12 that are interested in starting a new live bee program or strengthening an existing educational bee program. Applicants can select between the monetary and equipment options depending on their program needs. Traditional Bee Grant Options at a Glance Grant option Support provided Monetary Grant $2,000 to build and support a live bee program Equipment Grant Indoor Observation Hive plus $1,000 stipend The Traditional Bee Grant can therefore be useful for institutions that are at different stages of developing their bee education activities. A school starting from the beginning may need financial resources to build its program, while another institution may benefit more from having an indoor observation hive that can be incorporated directly into classroom learning. What Is the Renewal Bee Grant? The Renewal Bee Grant is designed specifically for previous Bee Grant recipients. Unlike the Traditional Bee Grant, which is intended for new applicants, the Renewal Bee Grant helps existing Bee Grant programs continue developing their educational bee initiatives. Previous recipients can use the funding to strengthen, expand, or refresh their existing bee programs. Renewal Grant recipients receive a $2,000 monetary grant to support the continued growth and development of their Bee Program. Who Can Apply for the Renewal Bee Grant? To qualify for the Renewal Bee Grant, an applicant must meet specific previous-recipient requirements. Applicants must have: Received a Traditional Bee Grant from the Whole Foods Market Foundation in 2025 or earlier . Completed the required Bee Grant Progress Report . An important feature of the Renewal Bee Grant is that live bees are not required in order to apply . This means previous grant recipients can seek renewal support even if their current program does not have live bees at the time of application. Additional Support Available to Renewal Grant Recipients The Renewal Bee Grant goes beyond financial assistance. Recipients can also benefit from additional resources intended to help them maintain and improve their educational bee programs. One-on-One Program Consultation Renewal recipients receive personalized support from The Bee Cause Project . This consultation can assist with areas such as: Program development Technical questions Program planning Beekeeping guidance where applicable Strategies for strengthening the educational value of the program This support can be particularly useful for organizations that have already established a bee program but want guidance on maintaining or expanding it. Educator Resource Pack Renewal Grant recipients also receive an educator resource package containing practical materials to support a strong and sustainable Bee Program. Resources can include: Standards-aligned lessons and activities Digital learning experiences Budgeting and planning tools Community engagement opportunities Additional educational resources These materials can help educators connect bee education to broader learning objectives and create a more structured long-term program. How the Bee Grant Supports STEAM Education One of the central educational benefits of the Bee Grant is its connection to STEAM learning . Students can use the study of honey bees and pollinators to explore concepts across multiple academic areas, including science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics. For example, students may learn about: Pollination and plant reproduction Honey bee behavior Ecosystems and biodiversity Environmental conservation Agricultural systems Habitat development Observation and data collection Problem-solving Scientific inquiry Sustainable environmental practices Because students can interact with a real or observation-based hive environment, educators have opportunities to connect theoretical lessons with practical experiences. Educational Resources for Bee Grant Applicants The Bee Cause Project provides resources that can help educators prepare for and develop their bee programs. The organization recommends building an educational foundation before introducing live bees. Its Back to School Bee Program provides resources that can be used by educators at different levels of experience, including educators who are completely new to bee education. The resources are designed to support distance learning, include teacher companion guides, and are mapped to educational standards. Step One: Educate The first recommended step is to establish a strong educational foundation. The Bee Cause Project recommends educators begin with its How to Grow Your Bee Program guide before implementing the Six Week Bee Unit. The Six Week Bee Unit provides educational materials such as: Standards-aligned lessons Teacher guides Flashcards Literature circle prompts These resources can help students develop an understanding of bees and pollinators before the institution introduces or expands a live bee program. Step Two: Build a Bee Club The second recommended step is to establish a Bee Club . A Bee Club can provide structure for students, educators, and members of the wider school community who want to learn more about bees. It can serve as a platform for activities such as: Bee-related book discussions Pollinator education Campus habitat development Learning about beekeeping Student-led environmental activities Community engagement Creating a Bee Club can also help an institution build broader support for its bee program. Step Three: Connect With the Community The Bee Cause Project encourages schools and organizations to connect their bee programs with their surrounding communities. Potential community connections can include: 4-H agents Local beekeeper associations Farmers Parents Educators Environmental organizations Other community members with knowledge of pollinators Community members can participate through in-person visits, educational sessions, and digital field trips. These interactions can provide students with perspectives beyond the classroom while helping families and community members better understand pollinators and the purpose of the school s bee program. Step Four: Expand Pollinator Habitat A successful bee program is not only about keeping bees. The Bee Cause Project also emphasizes the importance of healthy habitat. Schools and organizations can explore ways to create environments that support pollinators. This may involve: Developing native pollinator gardens Improving campus habitat Planting appropriate vegetation Teaching students about local ecosystems Learning how pollinators interact with plants Creating educational conservation projects The Bee a Friend to Pollinators lesson plan can help educators introduce students to the relationship between pollinators and their surrounding habitats. Preparing for the 2027 Bee Grant Application Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing before submitting their final applications. The Bee Cause Project makes previous application materials available as planning resources so prospective applicants can understand the type of information they may need to provide. For the Traditional Bee Grant, applicants can review the previous 2026 Traditional Bee Grant application while preparing for the 2027 application cycle. However, applicants should note that the previous application is provided as a preparation tool. All final 2027 Bee Grant applications must be submitted online. Applicants should therefore avoid relying solely on a downloaded or previous-year application and should complete the official application through the designated online platform. How to Apply for the 2027 Bee Grant Applications are submitted online through the SmartSimple platform . The general application process involves accessing the online platform, registering the school or organization, and completing the relevant Bee Grant application. Applicants should make sure they select the appropriate grant type: Traditional Bee Grant for eligible new applicants. Renewal Bee Grant for qualifying previous Bee Grant recipients. Applicants should also prepare the information and materials needed to explain their educational bee program and how the grant support will contribute to their students and organization. 2027 Bee Grant Application Deadline The application period for both the Traditional Bee Grant and Renewal Bee Grant opens on September 1 and closes on October 31 . Applicants should submit their completed applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Because online application platforms can experience technical issues or require additional registration steps, organizations interested in the grant may benefit from beginning the application process early. Bee Grant Application Webinars and Information Sessions The Bee Cause Project provides webinars and informational resources to help prospective applicants understand the program. The 2027 Bee Grant Overview Webinar covers areas such as: Eligibility Grant costs Application timelines Program information Other important considerations for applicants The organization also provides access to previous Bee Grant webinars and question-and-answer resources to help applicants prepare for the grant season. Prospective applicants should also monitor the Bee Cause Project s official channels for announcements concerning current-year webinars and live Q A sessions. Important Considerations for Applicants Before applying, schools and nonprofit organizations should carefully consider the practical requirements of running an educational bee program. These may include: Identifying educators who will oversee the program Establishing appropriate safety procedures Determining where educational hive equipment will be located Planning how students will interact with the program Identifying potential local beekeeping or community partners Developing lessons around the hive Considering habitat and environmental needs Planning how the program can be sustained beyond the grant period For applicants pursuing a new bee program, planning is particularly important because the grant represents an opportunity to establish an educational initiative that can continue serving students over time. APPLY HERE Why Schools May Consider Developing a Bee Education Program A live or observation-based bee program can provide a learning environment where students engage directly with environmental topics. Rather than studying pollination solely through textbooks, students can observe aspects of a working hive and use those observations as a basis for classroom discussion and inquiry. A school bee program can potentially support: Environmental education Conservation awareness STEAM learning Experiential learning Student engagement Community participation Pollinator habitat development Long-term sustainability education The program can also help students understand the connection between pollinators, plants, agriculture, ecosystems, and human communities. Visit HERE to learn more about the 2027 Bee Grant Program. Conclusion The 2027 Bee Grant Program provides schools and nonprofit organizations with an opportunity to introduce students to honey bees, pollinators, environmental conservation, and hands-on STEAM learning. The Traditional Bee Grant offers new applicants a choice between a $2,000 monetary grant and an equipment package consisting of an indoor observation hive and a $1,000 stipend . Meanwhile, previous qualifying Bee Grant recipients can apply for the Renewal Bee Grant , which provides $2,000 along with program consultation and educator resources. Beyond the financial and equipment support, the program provides access to educational materials, lesson plans, digital learning resources, planning tools, and other resources that can help educators build a structured and sustainable bee education program. Eligible schools and nonprofit organizations in the United States and Canada should take note of the application timeline. Applications for the 2027 Traditional and Renewal Bee Grants open on September 1 and close on October 31 . Organizations interested in applying should review the available preparation resources, determine which grant option applies to them, prepare their program information, and complete the final application through the official online SmartSimple platform before the deadline. title: University of South Wales PhD Studentship in Social Policy 2027 | Funded PhD Opportunity
summary: The University of South Wales is inviting applications from outstanding aspiring researchers for a funded PhD studentship in Social Policy for 2027 entry. The studentship provides an opportunity for researchers interested in social and public policy to develop an original research project within a broad and interdisciplinary research environment. Applicants are encouraged to propose research connected to areas including international development, global social policy, displacement and refugees, humanitarian development, geopolitics of energy, climate change, citizen involvement and participation, governance and scrutiny, equality, and social justice. The University also welcomes applications exploring the intersection of social policy with related areas in social care, the arts, humanities and creative industries. University of South Wales PhD Studentship in Social Policy The funded doctoral opportunity is designed for aspiring researchers who want to undertake advanced research in the broad field of social policy. Social policy research can address some of the major social, economic, political and environmental challenges facing communities and societies. The University of South Wales is particularly welcoming applications that connect social and public policy with contemporary issues such as inequality, climate change, displacement, governance, humanitarian development and global social policy. Applicants are encouraged to develop research proposals that demonstrate a clear research focus and connection with the University s areas of research expertise. Research Areas The studentship welcomes applications in a wide range of social and public policy areas. Potential areas include: International development Global social policy Displacement and refugees Humanitarian development Geopolitics of energy Climate change Citizen involvement and participation Governance and scrutiny Equality and social justice The University also welcomes research examining the intersection of social policy with cognate areas such as: Social care Arts Humanities Creative industries This interdisciplinary scope gives prospective applicants an opportunity to develop research topics that connect social policy with related academic and societal issues. Who Should Apply? The opportunity is intended for outstanding aspiring researchers who wish to pursue doctoral-level research in social policy or closely related areas. Applicants should consider how their proposed research fits within the University s research interests and should identify potential supervisors whose expertise aligns with their research topic. The source specifically encourages prospective applicants to explore the University s research areas and contact potential supervisors before applying. Research Topics and Interdisciplinary Opportunities One of the notable features of this PhD opportunity is the broad scope of potential research topics. Applicants could explore questions surrounding international development and global social policy, for example, or investigate issues affecting displaced populations and refugees. Other potential research directions include humanitarian development, climate change, energy geopolitics, governance, citizen participation, equality and social justice. Research proposals may also examine connections between social policy and social care, the arts, humanities or creative industries. This means applicants are not limited to a narrowly defined social policy topic. Instead, the opportunity provides scope for research that addresses important contemporary challenges through an interdisciplinary perspective. Contact Potential Supervisors Prospective applicants are encouraged to identify potential supervisors and explore the University s research expertise in their intended area before submitting an application. For a general enquiry or an informal discussion about a potential research topic, applicants can contact Professor Palash Kamruzzaman: palash.kamruzzaman@southwales.ac.uk For advice specifically relating to the application process, applicants can contact Ms Alison Crudgington in the Graduate School: gradschool@southwales.ac.uk Applicants should use these contacts to clarify questions about their proposed research topic or the application process before the deadline. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the University of South Wales funded PhD studentship in Social Policy is: 11 December 2026 Applicants should prepare their research proposal and application materials well in advance of the deadline to allow sufficient time for reviewing their documents and contacting potential supervisors. The source confirms 11 December 2026 as the application deadline. How to Prepare Your Application Prospective applicants should begin by identifying a research topic that fits within the broad social and public policy areas supported by the studentship. A strong preparation process can include: Identify your research area Choose a research topic connected to social policy, public policy or one of the related research areas listed by the University. Develop your research idea Clearly define the issue you want to investigate and consider the research questions your doctoral project could address. Explore potential supervisors Review the University s research expertise and identify academics whose research interests align with your proposed topic. Discuss your research topic Where appropriate, contact a potential supervisor or the relevant University contact to discuss your proposed research area. Review the application requirements Make sure you understand the University s application process and prepare the required documents before submitting your application. Submit before the deadline Ensure that your completed application is submitted by 11 December 2026. Why Consider This PhD Opportunity? A funded doctoral studentship can provide aspiring researchers with an opportunity to develop specialist expertise through advanced research. For applicants interested in social policy, the broad research scope of this opportunity may allow them to investigate important questions related to inequality, development, displacement, climate change, governance, participation and social justice. The interdisciplinary nature of the research areas may also be relevant to applicants whose interests connect social policy with social care, arts, humanities or creative industries. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully examine the research areas and determine whether their proposed project fits the scope of the studentship. Applicants should also consider contacting the University early enough to discuss their research topic and identify potential supervisory expertise. For application-process advice, contact the Graduate School at gradschool@southwales.ac.uk . For a general enquiry or informal discussion about a potential research topic, contact Professor Palash Kamruzzaman at palash.kamruzzaman@southwales.ac.uk . Conclusion The University of South Wales PhD Studentship in Social Policy offers an opportunity for aspiring researchers to pursue funded doctoral research across a broad range of social and public policy themes. Research interests may include international development, global social policy, displacement and refugees, humanitarian development, energy geopolitics, climate change, citizen participation, governance, equality and social justice. Applications connecting social policy with social care, arts, humanities and creative industries are also welcomed. Prospective applicants should explore the University s research areas, consider potential supervisors, seek application advice where necessary and prepare their applications before the 11 December 2026 deadline. title: Bennington College Young Scientists Awards 2026 | Win Up to $2,000
summary: The Bennington College Young Scientists Awards are inviting high school students from around the world to showcase original and creative work demonstrating scientific curiosity, critical thinking and engagement with the natural world. The awards are designed to recognize exceptional students in grades 9–12 whose work demonstrates originality, curiosity and scientific inquiry. Students can submit original work in the Natural Sciences category for the opportunity to receive cash prizes, recognition, publication and showcase opportunities. The competition is free to enter, and eligible students worldwide can participate. Cash prizes are available up to $2,000, while students who later enroll at Bennington College may also be eligible for significant scholarship opportunities. Bennington College Young Scientists Awards 2026 The Young Scientists Awards celebrate the next generation of scientists and encourage students to explore the natural world through observation, questioning, experimentation and creative expression. Bennington College is looking for work that challenges conventions, explores new ideas and demonstrates a distinct personal point of view. Students may explore topics ranging from pollinator diversity and local ecosystems to plant growth, environmental phenomena and other aspects of the natural world. The competition emphasizes creativity, thoughtfulness and a willingness to investigate questions rather than simply reproduce established information. Who Can Apply? The awards are open to students who meet the following requirements: Students in grades 9–12. Students from anywhere in the world. Students who have not yet graduated from high school. Students whose submissions are original work. Students whose entries are reviewed and approved by a sponsoring teacher or mentor. There is no entry fee. Only one submission in this discipline award is permitted per student. Important AI Requirement Applicants must pay particular attention to Bennington College s rules concerning artificial intelligence. All submissions are reviewed for authenticity and originality. The competition does not permit AI tools to be used to brainstorm, create, draft, revise or collaborate on any part of a submission. Entries that use AI will be disqualified from the Young Scientists Awards and may instead only be considered for the Young Innovators Awards. Students should therefore ensure that their submitted work is entirely their own. Submission Category: Natural Sciences The Young Scientists Awards include a Natural Sciences category. Students are asked to submit a visual illustration reflecting their specific or unique understanding of an aspect of the natural world. The submission may communicate: A scientific concept An element or aspect of nature Original research A scientific observation A research proposal A process or scientific explanation The goal is to create a personally crafted work that demonstrates knowledge and appreciation of natural science. What Can Students Submit? The competition provides several examples of possible submissions. Students could create a field guide documenting natural features in their local community, including: Animals Insects Flowers Trees Geology Topography Hydrology Other possibilities include a scientific illustration, drawing, painting or other visual representation of a natural subject such as a plant, bird or insect. Students may also create a poster explaining a scientific concept, natural phenomenon or research proposal. Such a poster could incorporate original research, a structural plan or a community proposal designed to improve local understanding, appreciation or preservation of the natural world. Another option is a process diagram or illustrated figure explaining an aspect of the natural world, preferably one connected to the student s direct experience. Optional Written Explanation Students may accompany their submission with an optional written explanation of up to 500 words. This explanation is intended to provide context and clarity about the work that was created. Students should use this space primarily to explain their submission rather than simply describing the scientific principles behind it, except where those principles influenced the creation of the work. Submission Requirements Entries must meet Bennington College s submission requirements. Submissions should be provided as one or more PDFs or digital photographs of the work. Accepted image formats include: JPEG JPG PNG TIFF Students may submit up to five images of their work. However, the competition notes that one high-resolution image may often be more effective than several lower-quality images. Physical copies of original artwork cannot be considered or returned. Sponsoring Teacher or Mentor All entries must be reviewed and approved by a high school sponsor teacher. The sponsoring teacher will serve as a contact for the competition if Bennington College has questions about the student s submission. Homeschooled students can contact a mentor to sponsor their work. Special Requirement for Grade 12 Students Grade 12 students have a different submission process. They must submit through either: The Common Application The Coalition Application The provided information states that these applications have no application fees, are non-binding and do not require supplemental essays. After completing the relevant application, students will receive a follow-up email containing instructions for submitting their Young Creators Awards entry. This approach allows students who are also applying to Bennington College to manage their college and awards applications through a single process. How Entries Are Evaluated Every submission is reviewed by a panel consisting of Bennington faculty and advanced students. The review process considers: Originality Quality of the work Engagement with complexity The competition also evaluates whether a submission demonstrates a distinct personal point of view and whether the work engages meaningfully with a challenging subject rather than relying on an easy or superficial approach. Judging Criteria The stated judging criteria include: Originality and Quality Judges consider the originality and quality of the final work. Personal Point of View Submissions should demonstrate the student s own perspective and interpretation. Engagement with Complexity Students are encouraged to address difficult questions and demonstrate meaningful engagement with the subject rather than settling for an overly simple presentation. Cash Prizes The Young Scientists Awards provide cash prizes in each category. The prizes are: First place: $2,000 Second place: $1,000 Third place: $500 There is also a Distinguished designation, which comes with a $250 award for particularly strong original submissions that are recognized for their quality but are not selected for one of the top three composition prizes. Scholarships for Bennington College The awards can also provide scholarship opportunities for students who later enroll at Bennington College. According to the provided information: First Place Winners who enroll at Bennington receive a full-tuition scholarship for four years. Distinguished Designation recipients who enroll receive a half-tuition scholarship for four years. Finalists who enroll receive a $25,000 annual scholarship for four years. Publication and Showcase Opportunities Winning and distinguished entries may also receive additional recognition. Selected work may be featured through: Bennington College s website Social media channels Publications Other showcase opportunities throughout the year The submitted work remains the property of the student. Important Dates The Young Scientists Awards follow the following timeline: September 1: Submissions open November 1: Submission deadline November–December: Round 1 judging by faculty and student panel January: Round 2 judging by external panel and selection of winners Spring: Award winners announced, press release issued, and winning entries published or showcased The submission period runs from September 1 at 9:00 AM ET through November 1 at 11:59 PM ET. How to Apply Eligible students should prepare an original Natural Sciences submission that reflects their understanding of a particular aspect of the natural world. Applicants should: Develop an original project. Ensure that the work demonstrates personal creativity and scientific inquiry. Avoid using AI at any stage of the submission process. Have the work reviewed and approved by a sponsoring teacher or mentor. Prepare the submission as a PDF or suitable digital image format. Submit no more than one entry in this discipline award. Complete the appropriate online submission process before the deadline. Grade 9–11 students can use the designated Young Creators Awards submission process, while Grade 12 students must follow the Common Application or Coalition Application process before receiving further submission instructions. Why Consider the Young Scientists Awards? The awards provide high school students with an opportunity to publicly demonstrate their scientific creativity and independent thinking. Beyond the possibility of receiving cash prizes, students can gain recognition for original scientific work and may have their work published or showcased by Bennington College. The competition can also provide scholarship opportunities for students who subsequently enroll at Bennington College. Conclusion The Bennington College Young Scientists Awards provide an international platform for high school students to demonstrate creativity, curiosity and scientific inquiry through original work focused on the natural sciences. Students in grades 9–12 from around the world can participate without paying an entry fee. Eligible students can submit original visual work such as scientific illustrations, field guides, research posters, process diagrams and other creative representations of the natural world. The competition offers cash prizes of up to $2,000, additional recognition through the Distinguished designation, publication and showcase opportunities, and scholarship opportunities for students who later enroll at Bennington College. Students interested in participating should carefully review the submission requirements, secure approval from a sponsoring teacher or mentor and ensure that no AI is used in any part of their submission. The submission deadline is November 1 at 11:59 PM ET. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: MARC Impact Programme 2026: High-Impact Enterprise Scaling Programme for Social Enterprises and Startups in 7 European Countries
summary: The MARC Impact Programme is a high-impact enterprise scaling initiative designed to support businesses that combine social or ecological impact with sustainable business growth . The programme is aimed at social enterprises, startups, nonprofit-developed businesses and for-profit companies seeking to develop an impact-oriented business arm. The initiative provides an opportunity for eligible enterprises to strengthen their business models, develop their impact potential and scale their operations while maintaining a strong focus on both commercial sustainability and positive social or environmental outcomes. According to the programme s application information, eligible applicants must be legally registered entities based in one of seven participating European countries: Austria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia or Serbia . What Is the MARC Impact Programme? MARC is described as a High-Impact Enterprise Scaling Programme , developed as a joint initiative involving ERSTE Foundation, ERSTE Social Finance Holding, IFUA Nonprofit Partner and SIMPACT . The programme is intended for businesses that do not view financial performance and social or environmental impact as competing priorities. Instead, applicants are expected to demonstrate that they are committed to building sustainable enterprises while creating measurable positive impact. The programme is particularly relevant to organizations that have moved beyond the earliest idea stage and are looking to strengthen their operations, business model, market position and capacity to grow their impact. The programme s application page states that it is looking for enterprises that: Have a clear social or ecological mission. Recognize the importance of both impact and business success. Have an established legal entity in one of the eligible countries. Already generate revenue or have a credible go-to-market strategy. Have a capable team supporting the business. Are committed to business growth and increasing their impact. Are prepared to dedicate time to the development process. Who Can Apply to the MARC Impact Programme? The programme is not designed for individual applicants applying in their personal capacity. Instead, it targets businesses and organizations with an established enterprise model and a social or environmental impact dimension . Several types of organizations can potentially apply. 1. Social Enterprises and Startups Social enterprises and startups with a clearly defined ecological or social mission are among the expected applicant groups. This means the business should have an identifiable purpose beyond generating financial returns. Its products, services or operations should contribute to addressing a social or environmental challenge. Examples may include enterprises working on areas such as: Environmental sustainability Circular economy Climate-related solutions Social inclusion Employment and livelihoods Education Community development Access to essential services Sustainable production Other measurable social or ecological challenges The important consideration is that the enterprise should have a genuine impact orientation alongside its business activities. 2. Businesses Developed Within Nonprofits Organizations that originated within nonprofit institutions can also fall within the programme s target applicant group. A nonprofit may, for example, have developed a business or revenue-generating activity designed to address a social or environmental challenge. Such an enterprise can potentially be considered where it has developed sufficiently as a business and meets the programme s other requirements. 3. For-Profit Businesses Developing an Impact Arm The programme also welcomes for-profit businesses that want to develop an impact arm. This is particularly relevant to established companies that want to introduce or strengthen a component of their operations dedicated to generating measurable social or ecological impact. Rather than requiring every applicant to be structured exclusively as a social enterprise, the programme therefore recognizes that conventional businesses can also develop impact-oriented activities. Key Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully consider the programme s eligibility requirements before starting an application. 1. The Organization Must Be Legally Registered One of the central requirements is that the applicant must be a legally registered entity . The organization must also be based in one of the programme s seven eligible countries. These are: Austria Croatia Czechia Hungary Romania Slovakia Serbia Organizations located outside these countries are not identified as eligible under the application criteria provided on the programme website. 2. The Business Should Have a Social or Ecological Mission The programme is intended for enterprises that combine business activity with an identifiable impact mission. Applicants should therefore be able to clearly explain: What social or environmental problem they are addressing. How their business contributes to solving that problem. Who benefits from their work. How their solution creates impact. How the enterprise intends to expand that impact as it grows. A strong application should demonstrate a clear relationship between the organization s business model and its intended impact. 3. Impact and Business Success Should Both Matter Applicants are expected to believe that impact and business success are equally important . This requirement is significant because MARC is not simply an impact-focused initiative seeking organizations based only on the strength of their social mission. The programme also looks for enterprises with a viable business perspective. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate how they intend to achieve both: Sustainable business growth; and Increased social or ecological impact. 4. Revenue or a Solid Go-to-Market Plan The application criteria indicate that an enterprise should either: Already generate revenue; or Have a solid go-to-market plan. This suggests that the programme is intended for businesses that have progressed beyond simply having an undeveloped concept. Organizations already generating revenue can demonstrate market validation through their existing operations. For businesses that have not yet generated significant revenue, a credible go-to-market strategy can demonstrate that they have a realistic plan for bringing their product or service to customers or beneficiaries. A go-to-market plan may cover areas such as: Target customers Target markets Product or service positioning Pricing strategy Sales channels Marketing strategy Customer acquisition Market expansion Revenue projections Partnerships and distribution 5. A Well-Equipped Team The programme also expects applicants to have a well-equipped team behind the business . This means the organization should be supported by people capable of executing its strategy and managing its growth. Applicants should be able to demonstrate relevant capabilities within their team, including areas such as: Leadership Business development Operations Finance Marketing and communications Product or service development Impact measurement Partnership development A strong team can help demonstrate that the enterprise has the capacity to make effective use of the programme s development opportunities. 6. Commitment to Business Growth Applicants must be committed to growing their business in order to accelerate their impact. The programme therefore looks beyond enterprises that simply want to maintain their current operations. Applicants should have a clear ambition to expand their activities and increase the scale of their positive social or ecological contribution. This could involve: Reaching more customers or beneficiaries. Entering new markets. Expanding products or services. Increasing revenue. Developing new partnerships. Increasing employment. Expanding geographical coverage. Improving impact measurement. Scaling an existing solution. 7. Willingness to Invest Time in the Development Process Participation requires a meaningful commitment of time. Applicants are expected to be willing to invest their time in the development process associated with the programme. This is important because enterprise scaling requires active participation from founders, managers and other key team members. Organizations considering applying should therefore ensure that the appropriate members of their team have sufficient time and capacity to participate. Eligible Countries for the MARC Impact Programme The MARC Impact Programme currently identifies seven countries from which eligible entities can apply. Austria Organizations legally registered and based in Austria can apply through the designated Austria application process. Croatia Eligible Croatian entities can submit their application through the programme s Croatia application channel. Czechia Organizations based in Czechia are included among the programme s eligible applicants. Hungary Hungarian enterprises meeting the programme requirements can apply through the designated Hungary programme. Romania Legally registered organizations based in Romania are also included among the eligible applicants. Serbia Serbian enterprises that meet the programme requirements can apply through the designated Serbia application process. Slovakia Organizations legally registered and based in Slovakia are also eligible to apply, subject to meeting the remaining criteria. title: 2026 Impact Grant: €50,000 in Unrestricted Funding for Arts Nonprofits Supporting Underrepresented Emerging Artists
summary: The 2026 Impact Grant by The Supporting Act Foundation is an opportunity for eligible nonprofit arts organizations that are working to support emerging artists from underrepresented groups and communities facing systemic barriers in the creative and cultural industries. The grant is specifically designed for organizations that provide non-financial support to emerging artists. Rather than funding individual artists or specific projects, the Impact Grant supports nonprofit organizations whose ongoing work helps artists develop their practices, improve their living conditions, gain greater visibility, and build confidence in their creative careers. For the 2026 funding cycle, 10 organizations will receive unrestricted grants of €25,000 per year for two years, providing a total of €50,000 per selected organization . Applications are open to eligible nonprofit arts organizations based in Belgium, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, and the United Kingdom, as well as organizations registered elsewhere that work with an eligible fiscal host. The application deadline is October 1, 2026, at 11:00 AM CET . About the 2026 Impact Grant The Impact Grant is an initiative of The Supporting Act Foundation , which seeks to support organizations contributing to meaningful change in the creative and cultural sector. The 2026 grant focuses on nonprofit arts organizations that work with underrepresented emerging artists . These may be artists who face systemic barriers to accessing opportunities, visibility, professional development, networks, resources, or other forms of support within the creative and cultural industries. The program recognizes that emerging artists often need more than direct financial assistance. Organizations can play an important role by providing mentoring, professional development, platforms for visibility, community-building opportunities, access to networks, guidance, and other forms of non-financial support. Through the Impact Grant, The Supporting Act Foundation aims to strengthen organizations that are already doing this work and help them increase their long-term impact. The program s intended impact includes: Improving the living conditions of artists. Enabling emerging artists to dedicate more time to developing their artistic practices. Increasing the visibility of artists and their work. Supporting artists who face systemic barriers within the creative and cultural industries. Strengthening artists confidence in their work and professional development. Supporting nonprofit organizations that create meaningful opportunities for underrepresented artists. Helping organizations sustain and expand their contribution to the arts ecosystem. What Does the 2026 Impact Grant Provide? The 2026 Impact Grant will provide 10 unrestricted grants . Each selected nonprofit organization will receive: €25,000 per year Funding for two years €50,000 total per organization Unrestricted funding intended to support the organization s work rather than a specific project proposal The unrestricted nature of the funding is particularly relevant for organizations that require flexibility to respond to the needs of the artists and communities they serve. Instead of restricting the grant to one predetermined project, unrestricted support can give eligible organizations greater flexibility in strengthening their existing work and organizational activities. A total of 10 nonprofit organizations will be selected for the 2026 Impact Grant. Who Is the 2026 Impact Grant For? The Impact Grant is intended for nonprofit arts organizations , rather than individual artists. Eligible organizations should have an established focus on supporting emerging artists from underrepresented groups or artists who experience systemic barriers to opportunities in the creative and cultural industries. Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that their organization is actively providing non-financial support to emerging artists. Examples of such support may include professional development, mentoring, artistic platforms, networking opportunities, community support, visibility initiatives, career guidance, capacity building, or other forms of assistance that do not constitute direct financial grants to artists. Organizations should be able to demonstrate this work through publicly available information on their websites. 2026 Impact Grant Eligibility Criteria Organizations interested in applying must satisfy the eligibility requirements established by The Supporting Act Foundation. 1. The applicant must be a nonprofit arts organization The opportunity is intended specifically for nonprofit organizations operating within the arts and cultural sector. Organizations must have been registered as a nonprofit arts organization between 2016 and 2024 . The organization must also be registered in one of the eligible countries listed below. 2. The organization must be based in an eligible country The applicant organization must be registered in one of the following countries: Belgium France Germany Greece Ireland Italy The Netherlands Portugal Spain United Kingdom Organizations registered outside these countries may also be eligible if they can provide a letter of intent from a fiscal host that is registered as a nonprofit organization in one of the eligible countries. This means that organizations outside the listed countries should not automatically assume that they are excluded. However, they must meet the fiscal-host requirement specified by the program. 3. A qualifying bank account is required Applicants must be able to provide a bank account number with an IBAN in the name of either: The applicant organization; or An eligible fiscal host located in one of the listed countries. Organizations should ensure that they can meet this requirement before beginning the application process. 4. The organization must meet the annual expenditure requirement Eligible organizations must have a total annual expenditure of between €50,000 and €300,000 , or the equivalent amount in the organization s local currency, during the current fiscal year. This requirement is intended to ensure that applicants have an established level of organizational activity and financial operations. Organizations should therefore review their current financial information before applying. 5. The organization must have an updated website Applicants must have an updated website that provides publicly available evidence of the organization s active work. The website should demonstrate that the organization provides non-financial support to emerging artists from underrepresented groups or to artists facing systemic barriers to opportunities in the creative and cultural industries. This makes the organization s online presence an important part of demonstrating eligibility. Applicants should ensure that their website clearly communicates: What the organization does. Who it supports. How it supports emerging artists. The communities or groups it works with. Examples of active or recent programs. Evidence of its contribution to the creative and cultural sector. Current The Supporting Act Foundation grantees. Past The Supporting Act Foundation grantees. The grant is focused on eligible nonprofit arts organizations rather than individual creative projects. Instead, organizations may support artists through activities and services that help them build sustainable creative careers. This could include areas such as: Mentorship. Professional development. Artistic development. Training. Networking. Career guidance. Exhibitions and showcases. Performance opportunities. Community-building. Access to professional networks. Platforms that increase artists visibility. Creative workshops. Knowledge-sharing. Industry connections. Support for artists facing systemic barriers. Opportunities to develop and present artistic work. Applicants should focus on demonstrating what their organization actually does and the impact its support has on emerging artists. An artist may have the creative ability and ambition to develop professionally but still lack access to networks, mentorship, platforms, professional opportunities, training, or visibility. Arts nonprofits can help address these gaps by creating supportive environments where emerging artists can develop their skills and practices. The Impact Grant is designed around this broader understanding of impact. The Supporting Act Foundation identifies several desired outcomes, including improving artists living conditions, giving artists more time to develop their practices, increasing the visibility of their work, and strengthening their confidence. For nonprofit organizations already working in these areas, the grant provides an opportunity to strengthen their organizational capacity and continue their work over a two-year funding period. Each selected organization will receive: €25,000 per year for two years This amounts to: €50,000 total funding per selected organization. There will be: 10 grants available. Provides non-financial support to emerging artists from underrepresented groups or artists facing systemic barriers. Is not an excluded applicant type. title: Max Planck Institute Visiting Researchers Program 2027 | Research Opportunity in Germany
summary: The Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies (MPIfG) is inviting applications for its Visiting Researchers Program for the summer semester 2027. The program offers an opportunity for doctoral researchers, postdoctoral researchers and professors to spend between two and twelve months conducting research at the Institute in Cologne, Germany. The Visiting Researchers Program is intended for scholars working in the fields of economic sociology and comparative and international political economy. Applicants are expected to propose a research project that relates closely to the MPIfG’s research program and that they wish to pursue during their stay at the Institute. The Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies conducts basic research into the governance of modern societies. Its research seeks to develop empirically based theories of the social and political foundations of modern economies by examining the relationships between social, economic and political action. Max Planck Institute Visiting Researchers Program 2027 The MPIfG Visiting Researchers Program provides scholars with an opportunity to become part of the Institute s academic environment and pursue an independent research project related to its research agenda. The Institute s research program draws particularly on sociology and political science and combines approaches from new economic sociology with comparative and international political economy. Visiting researchers will work in a collaborative academic environment and will be assigned to an MPIfG director or research group leader during their stay. Applicants are therefore required to identify a preferred MPIfG director or research group leader as part of their online application. Fields of Research The program is specifically open to scholars whose research falls within: Economic sociology Comparative political economy International political economy Applicants should ensure that their proposed research project has a clear connection to the MPIfG s research program. The Institute encourages research that relates to its broader interest in understanding the social, economic and political foundations of modern economies and the governance of modern societies. Duration of the Visiting Research Stay Visiting researchers can generally undertake stays ranging from: 2 months Up to 12 months The exact dates of an agreed visiting researcher stay must be carefully considered before applying. According to the program information, agreed dates cannot be postponed or split. If a successful applicant is subsequently unable to attend during the agreed period, they may reapply for the following year. Who Can Apply? The Visiting Researchers Program is open to: Professors Postdoctoral researchers Doctoral researchers Applications are welcome from scholars based in Germany as well as researchers from abroad. Applicants should have a research project that they wish to pursue at the MPIfG and that relates to the Institute s research program. Research Proposal Requirements A central component of the application is the research proposal. Applicants are expected to submit a research proposal of up to three pages outlining the project they intend to pursue during their time at the MPIfG. The proposal should clearly communicate the research project and demonstrate its relevance to the Institute s research program. Applicants should therefore carefully consider: The research question they intend to investigate. How the project relates to economic sociology or comparative and international political economy. Why conducting the research at the MPIfG would be relevant to the project. The proposed research activities during the visiting period. The academic contribution or objectives of the research. Funding for the Visiting Research Stay An important requirement of the program is that visiting researchers must provide their own funding. Applicants are required to submit a funding plan for their proposed stay. The MPIfG does not indicate in the provided announcement that the visiting researcher position itself provides funding. Instead, successful applicants receive a letter of invitation that they can use when approaching funding institutions. Researchers who require external financial support should therefore investigate suitable funding opportunities and develop their funding plans alongside their application. Academic Environment Successful visiting researchers become part of the MPIfG s collaborative and collegial working environment. During the program, each visiting researcher is assigned to an MPIfG director or research group leader. Applicants are asked to indicate their preferred director or research group leader in the online application. This allows applicants to identify an academic connection between their research interests and the Institute s research community. The program can therefore provide an opportunity for researchers to pursue their own projects while engaging with scholars working within the Institute. Selection Process Successful candidates are selected on the basis of: Scholarly excellence The quality and relevance of the proposed research project The connection between the proposed project and the MPIfG research program The research proposal can be up to three pages and should outline the project the applicant intends to pursue at the Institute. Because the MPIfG is a small research institute, only a limited number of visiting researcher positions can be offered each year. Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal is clearly developed and demonstrates a strong connection with the Institute s academic focus. Application Language Applications may be submitted in: English German The Institute states that applications must be submitted online. Applications sent by email will not be considered. Application Deadline The deadline for applications to the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies Visiting Researchers Program is: October 31, 2026 at 23:59 UTC+1 Applicants should ensure that their online application is completed and submitted before the stated deadline. How to Apply Interested researchers should prepare their application through the official MPIfG online application system. The application process involves presenting the proposed research project and identifying a preferred MPIfG director or research group leader. Applicants should also prepare their own funding plan because visiting researchers are expected to provide their own funding. The official application page should be used to submit the application. Applications sent by email are not accepted. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants can take several steps to prepare before submitting their application. 1. Identify a relevant research topic Develop a research project that falls within economic sociology or comparative and international political economy and has a clear connection to the MPIfG s research program. 2. Develop the research proposal Prepare a concise proposal of no more than three pages that clearly explains the project to be pursued during the visiting period. 3. Identify a suitable MPIfG research connection Review the Institute s research program and identify the director or research group leader whose expertise is most relevant to the proposed project. 4. Prepare a funding plan Because visiting researchers are expected to provide their own funding, applicants should identify possible funding institutions and develop a realistic plan for financing their stay. 5. Plan the visiting period carefully Applicants should consider the proposed dates carefully because agreed visiting periods cannot subsequently be postponed or divided. 6. Submit the application online Complete the online application in English or German before the October 31, 2026 deadline. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion The MPIfG states that it is committed to equality of opportunity and a diverse and inclusive working environment. The Institute welcomes applications from people of different backgrounds and highlights its commitment to equality of opportunity. It also identifies compatibility between career and family as an important concern and supports the employment of people with disabilities. Successful applicants receive an invitation letter that can be used when approaching funding institutions. Applicants should identify a preferred MPIfG director or research group leader. Applications can be submitted in English or German. Applications must be submitted online. Applications by email are not considered. The application deadline is October 31, 2026 at 23:59 UTC+1. Conclusion The Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies Visiting Researchers Program 2027 offers an opportunity for doctoral researchers, postdoctoral researchers and professors to pursue research within a leading academic environment focused on the governance of modern societies and the relationship between social, economic and political action.
