title: FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers 2026: Up to BRL 2.5 Million for Researchers to Establish Research Programs in Brazil
summary: The São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP) has launched the Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers 2026 , a major research funding opportunity designed to attract outstanding researchers from around the world to establish or consolidate independent research careers at leading higher education and research institutions in the State of São Paulo, Brazil. The international call seeks researchers with strong academic trajectories, internationally recognized expertise, demonstrated research achievements, and the potential to become scientific leaders in strategically important fields. Under the 2026 call, FAPESP plans to support up to 20 outstanding researchers , with successful projects receiving funding of up to BRL 2.5 million per proposal . A Young Investigator Fellowship may also be requested in addition to this funding limit. Research projects will have a duration of 60 months , providing successful researchers with substantial time and resources to establish laboratories, build research teams, develop independent research programs, and pursue internationally competitive scientific work in São Paulo. Applications must be submitted by November 19, 2026 . About the FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers The Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers is an initiative of the São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP) . FAPESP is a public foundation of the State of São Paulo with a mission to support research across all fields of knowledge at higher education and research institutions throughout São Paulo. The Foundation operates in close collaboration with the scientific community, and research proposals submitted for FAPESP support undergo peer review involving specialists in relevant disciplines. Through this dedicated international call, FAPESP aims to strengthen São Paulo s scientific and technological leadership by attracting researchers currently based outside Brazil who have the expertise and potential to develop independent, high-impact research programs. The 2026 initiative is expected to support up to 20 researchers. Purpose of the 2026 International Call The central purpose of the FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers is to attract outstanding scientific talent from abroad to research institutions in São Paulo. FAPESP is seeking researchers who can establish or consolidate their research careers in the state while creating independent and internationally competitive research programs. The initiative is particularly focused on candidates who demonstrate: Outstanding expertise in their respective fields; Originality and independence in research; Strong scientific achievements following completion of their doctorate; Potential for scientific leadership; Ability to establish an independent research program; Capacity to create new research collaborations; Potential to conduct high-impact research; and A research trajectory demonstrating international competitiveness. Successful applicants are expected to establish a research laboratory and develop a dedicated research program at an institution located in the State of São Paulo. Research Areas Supported by the FAPESP Young Investigator Grant 2026 Projects submitted under this international call must fall within the strategic research themes identified by FAPESP. The eligible research areas are: Biotechnology Energy Transition Biodiversity, Sustainable Production and Food Security Digital Transition and Artificial Intelligence Quantum Science and Technology Human and Animal Health Public Security These fields reflect areas that FAPESP considers strategically important for strengthening scientific and technological development. Projects approved specifically under the artificial intelligence research theme will be affiliated with the recently established São Paulo Artificial Intelligence Research Center , which is supported by FAPESP, MCTI/CGI.br and São Paulo State Universities. Who Can Apply? The 2026 call is specifically designed to attract researchers who are currently living and working outside Brazil. Researchers of all nationalities may apply, provided they satisfy the program s eligibility requirements. Applicants must have been living and working abroad for at least two years after completing their PhD . Eligible professional experience abroad can include: Postdoctoral appointments; Research fellowships; Permanent academic positions; Permanent research positions; or Other qualifying appointments at research institutions. Applicants must also be residing abroad when they submit their proposals. The successful researcher is expected to relocate to São Paulo and establish or consolidate their research career at an eligible research institution in the state. Research Experience and Leadership Requirements Simply holding a PhD is not sufficient to make an application competitive. FAPESP expects applicants to demonstrate significant achievements since completing their doctoral studies. Their academic and research trajectory should provide evidence of: Original scientific contributions; Research independence; Leadership capacity; Scientific impact; International research experience; Ability to establish an independent research program; Capacity to build research collaborations; and Potential to undertake ambitious research at the frontier of knowledge. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding expertise and leadership within their respective fields through the quality, originality, relevance, and impact of their scientific achievements. Establishing a Research Program in São Paulo An important feature of the program is that successful researchers are not simply expected to conduct a temporary research visit in Brazil. Applicants should be prepared to establish a research laboratory and develop a dedicated research program at an institution in the State of São Paulo . Successful candidates are expected to become fully integrated into their host institutions and demonstrate a strong commitment to both the proposed project and their research position. This makes the program particularly relevant for international researchers seeking an opportunity to establish or consolidate an independent academic and scientific career in Brazil. Independent Research Requirement Competitive proposals must present a clearly defined and independent research line led by the applicant . Researchers may collaborate with established research groups on particular topics, and such collaborations are permitted and encouraged. However, the proposed project should demonstrate the applicant s own scientific independence and ability to lead an internationally competitive research program. This distinction is important because FAPESP is seeking researchers capable of developing new scientific directions rather than merely joining existing projects as supporting researchers. Funding Available One of the most significant features of the FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers 2026 is the scale of funding available. The maximum funding available per proposal is BRL 2,500,000 . This amount represents the maximum requested project budget under the call. Importantly, the Young Investigator Fellowship may be requested in addition to the BRL 2.5 million funding limit . Funding will follow the applicable FAPESP criteria and regulations for the Young Investigator Grant. Young Investigator Fellowship A Young Investigator Fellowship may be awarded for up to the full duration of the research grant. The fellowship can continue until the Principal Investigator obtains a permanent position at a university or research institution in the State of São Paulo. This arrangement is intended to provide researchers with support while they establish themselves within São Paulo s research ecosystem. During implementation of the project, Principal Investigators are encouraged to apply for permanent positions available at their host institution or other universities and research institutions within São Paulo. This creates a potential pathway toward a longer-term academic or research career in Brazil. Funding for Research Team Members Successful applicants may also request scholarships and fellowships for members of their research teams in accordance with the applicable FAPESP rules. Potential categories include: PhD scholarships; Master s scholarships; Scientific Initiation scholarships; Postdoctoral Fellowships; and Other eligible fellowship modalities under FAPESP rules. For this particular call, however, only one scholarship or fellowship of each modality can be included in a proposal . For each requested fellowship, the applicant must provide a one-page summary explaining the research objectives, work plan, and implementation schedule associated with that position. Relocation Support for International Researchers Successful applicants currently living abroad may also qualify for relocation support . According to the call, this can include airfare for the successful applicant in accordance with FAPESP s applicable relocation-support rules. This is particularly important because the program requires selected researchers to establish their research activities within the State of São Paulo rather than conducting the project remotely from another country. Number of Researchers to Be Supported FAPESP states that a maximum of 20 fellowships will be awarded under this international call. The program is therefore selective and aimed at researchers with particularly strong academic records and ambitious research proposals. Candidates should ensure that both their scientific track record and proposed research clearly demonstrate originality, impact, independence, and international competitiveness. Project Duration Research projects submitted under the program must have a duration of: 60 months This represents a five-year research period. Upon request and subject to evaluation by FAPESP, both the project and associated fellowship may potentially be extended by up to 12 additional months . The five-year structure provides researchers with substantial time to establish laboratories, recruit and develop research teams, generate scientific outputs, establish collaborations, and consolidate independent research programs. Potential Long-Term Career Pathway The program may also serve as a pathway toward longer-term academic and scientific careers within São Paulo. During implementation, Principal Investigators are encouraged to apply for available permanent positions at their host institution or other eligible universities and research institutions in the state. Researchers who obtain permanent positions after completing their projects may potentially continue their work through other FAPESP funding mechanisms. This can include the Young Investigator Grant – Phase 2 , provided the researcher satisfies the relevant eligibility criteria and successfully completes the applicable merit-review process. Documents Required for Application Applicants must prepare a comprehensive proposal package. 1. Short CV Candidates must submit a short CV in English of no more than five pages . It should include relevant researcher identification information, including: Scopus ID; Google Scholar profile; and Web of Science ResearcherID. Applicants must also provide a career summary of no more than 400 words . The CV should explain the applicant s most important scientific achievements and their relevance to the proposed research project. Candidates must identify their five most important publications , explaining their leadership role in the research and the scientific impact of those contributions. The CV must additionally identify the applicant s three most significant invited talks , academic degrees, and previous professional appointments. 2. Research Trajectory Letter Applicants must provide a letter of no more than two pages explaining how their research trajectory evolved toward the central concept underlying the proposed project. The letter should highlight significant findings, observations, scientific developments, and experiences that contributed to the development of the proposed research direction. 3. Research Project Applicants must submit a detailed research project demonstrating: Clearly defined objectives; Originality; Scientific ambition; Strong scientific rationale; Potential advances at the frontier of knowledge; International competitiveness; Feasibility of implementation; and The research team s capacity to complete the work successfully. The main body of the research project must not exceed 20 pages, including references , excluding annexes and supporting documents. 4. Fellowship Work Plans If scholarships or fellowships are requested for team members, applicants must clearly describe the activities associated with each position. A one-page summary must be submitted for every requested fellowship, including the research objectives, work plan, and implementation schedule. 5. Budget Information Applicants must enter requested budget items through FAPESP s SAGe system. Vendor quotations must be provided for capital equipment that will be purchased in Brazil or abroad when its value exceeds the threshold specified under FAPESP regulations. Language of Application Research proposals must be submitted in English . Applicants should therefore ensure that their scientific arguments, methodology, objectives, expected results, and broader research rationale are presented clearly and professionally in English. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through FAPESP s SAGe system . Applicants using the English interface should navigate through: New Proposal Special Programs YIG – Young Investigator Grant Grant for International Researchers Call for Proposals (2026) Candidates should prepare their documentation well before the deadline because the application involves several substantial components, including a research proposal, academic CV, research-trajectory letter, fellowship plans where applicable, and budget documentation. Evaluation Process The proposal submission and evaluation process consists of three major stages : Submission of the proposal; Evaluation by external reviewers and FAPESP s evaluation process; and Online presentation and interview for selected candidates. Initial Eligibility Assessment An Evaluation Committee will assess whether the applicant and proposed research align with the objectives and expected profile of the international Young Investigator Grant. The assessment considers factors including: Originality and innovation; Potential scientific impact; Potential societal impact; Scientific quality; Research relevance; Project feasibility; Potential contribution to advancing knowledge; Applicant s scientific background; Research achievements; and Career trajectory. Full Proposal Evaluation Full proposals will be sent to at least two external reviewers . A FAPESP evaluation panel will consider these assessments when reviewing the applications. Among the issues considered will be the project s potential impact on its field, its relationship to existing scientific work, and whether it provides new approaches to relevant research challenges. Reviewers and the evaluation panel will also consider the applicant s capacity to establish new strategic collaborations with research institutions at local, regional, and international levels while maintaining scientific independence. Interview Stage Candidates whose full proposals receive a positive recommendation may be invited to participate in an online oral presentation and interview with members of the Evaluation Committee. Applicants should therefore be prepared not only to submit a strong written proposal but also to explain and defend their proposed research program, its significance, methodology, feasibility, originality, and potential impact. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting full proposals is: November 19, 2026 Applicants should ensure that all required materials are submitted through the appropriate FAPESP system before the deadline. Results Announcement FAPESP expects the final results to be announced beginning in: June 2027 Successful projects should normally begin before December 2027 , except where exceptional circumstances apply. Key Dates at a Glance Call Announcement: September 2026 Full Proposal Deadline: November 19, 2026 Final Results: From June 2027 Expected Project Start: Before December 2027 Project Duration: 60 months Possible Extension: Up to 12 months, subject to request and FAPESP evaluation Why This Opportunity Matters for International Researchers The FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers represents more than short-term project financing. It provides successful researchers with the opportunity to establish an independent research program within one of Brazil s largest scientific and academic ecosystems. The combination of substantial research funding, a five-year project period, potential fellowship support, research-team scholarships, relocation assistance, and the possibility of pursuing permanent academic positions makes the program particularly relevant to internationally mobile researchers seeking to build independent scientific careers. The emphasis on independence is also important. FAPESP is looking for applicants capable of leading their own research directions and developing internationally competitive programs rather than simply participating in existing research activities. Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application Applicants should begin preparing well before the November deadline because the application requires extensive scientific and administrative documentation. Researchers should ensure that their proposals clearly demonstrate: Why the proposed research question matters; What makes the research original; How it advances the frontier of knowledge; Why the applicant is particularly well positioned to conduct the project; How the project differs from existing research; Whether the proposed methodology is scientifically rigorous and feasible; What scientific or societal impact could result; How the researcher will establish an independent research line; How the project could strengthen research capacity in São Paulo; and How the applicant s previous achievements demonstrate leadership potential. Applicants should also ensure that their CV, trajectory letter, and research proposal tell a coherent scientific story. Conclusion The FAPESP Young Investigator Grant for International Researchers 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for accomplished early-career and emerging independent researchers currently based outside Brazil to establish ambitious research programs in the State of São Paulo. With up to BRL 2.5 million in project funding , the possibility of an additional Young Investigator Fellowship, relocation support, research-team scholarships and fellowships, and a 60-month project duration , the program provides substantial resources for researchers seeking to build independent and internationally competitive scientific programs. Researchers from all nationalities may be considered, provided they satisfy the eligibility conditions, including having lived and worked abroad for at least two years after completing their PhD and being based abroad when submitting the application. Research proposals can address strategically important areas ranging from biotechnology and artificial intelligence to energy transition, quantum science, health, biodiversity, sustainable production, food security, and public security. Eligible researchers interested in establishing or consolidating their research careers in São Paulo should begin preparing their applications well ahead of the November 19, 2026 deadline . title: Global Futures Scholarships 2027 at the University of Manchester: More Than £6 Million in Funding for International Students
summary: The University of Manchester is offering a major scholarship opportunity for international students planning to begin undergraduate or master s studies in September 2027. Through the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 , the University is providing more than £6 million in scholarship awards , with more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships available for eligible international students. The scholarships are designed for international students who intend to study full-time and on campus at the University of Manchester in Manchester, United Kingdom. Applicants must first secure an offer of admission for an eligible course beginning in September 2027 before they can apply for the scholarship. Global Futures Scholarships 2027: Overview The Global Futures Scholarships provide international students with an opportunity to receive financial support towards their studies at one of the UK s major universities. For the 2027 entry cycle, the University of Manchester states that it is offering: More than £6 million in scholarship awards. More than 350 partial merit-based scholarships . Scholarships for both undergraduate students and master s students . Opportunities for eligible students from a specified list of countries. Scholarships for students beginning their studies in September 2027 . The scholarship is particularly relevant to international applicants who are preparing applications to the University of Manchester and are seeking financial support for their studies. What Are the Global Futures Scholarships? The Global Futures Scholarships are international student scholarships offered by the University of Manchester for students entering eligible undergraduate and postgraduate taught master s programmes. For 2027 entry, the University describes the awards as partial merit-based scholarships . This means the scholarships are intended to provide financial support based on merit, rather than representing a full scholarship covering every cost associated with studying in the United Kingdom. The University has allocated more than £6 million to the scholarship programme for international students starting their studies in September 2027. Because the programme covers multiple countries and regions, the exact award amount, eligibility requirements and application deadline are not necessarily identical for every applicant. The University specifically advises applicants to consult the scholarship information for their country because the award level, eligibility criteria and application deadlines differ by region . Who Can Apply for the Global Futures Scholarships 2027? The opportunity is open to eligible international students who meet the University s requirements. According to the University of Manchester, applicants must satisfy the following fundamental conditions: Be living in one of the countries covered by the scholarship. Hold an offer from the University of Manchester. Have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester . Be applying for a programme that starts in September 2027 . Complete the scholarship application process after receiving the relevant invitation from the University. The scholarship is available to applicants at both undergraduate and master s level, although the precise requirements may vary according to the applicant s country and level of study. Eligible Countries for the Global Futures Scholarships The University of Manchester has identified specific countries whose residents can be considered for the Global Futures Scholarships. The 2027 scholarship page lists the following countries: Bangladesh Botswana Canada Egypt Ghana India Indonesia Kenya Malaysia Mauritius Nigeria Pakistan Saudi Arabia Singapore South Africa Sri Lanka Taiwan Thailand Türkiye United Arab Emirates United States Vietnam Zimbabwe This makes the opportunity relevant to prospective international students across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, North America and other specified international markets . Applicants should pay particular attention to the country-specific information because eligibility conditions and application deadlines can vary from one country to another. Important note for applicants from Africa The countries listed from Africa include: Botswana Egypt Ghana Kenya Mauritius Nigeria South Africa Zimbabwe Therefore, applicants living in these countries can review their respective country profiles to determine the specific scholarship conditions applicable to them. Applicants should not assume that meeting the general scholarship conditions automatically guarantees eligibility, because the University indicates that individual country profiles contain specific criteria. Scholarships Available for Undergraduate and Master s Students One of the important features of the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 is that the programme covers more than one level of university study. The University states that there are more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships available for undergraduate and master s students entering in 2027. Undergraduate applicants International students seeking to begin an undergraduate programme at the University of Manchester in September 2027 may be eligible to apply, provided they satisfy the applicable country-specific requirements and have an offer for an eligible full-time, on-campus course. Applicants should therefore begin by researching suitable undergraduate programmes, checking their academic admission requirements and submitting their university application. Master s applicants The scholarship also provides opportunities for eligible international students planning to begin master s-level study in September 2027. Master s applicants must similarly hold an offer for an eligible full-time, on-campus course at the University of Manchester and satisfy the conditions applicable to their country. The supplied scholarship information also notes that Taiwan is listed for postgraduate taught master s only , making it important for applicants from each country to read their specific country profile carefully. What Does the Scholarship Cover? The Global Futures Scholarships are described by the University of Manchester as partial merit-based scholarships . The university s 2027 announcement confirms that the overall scholarship programme has a value exceeding £6 million , with more than 350 awards available. However, the supplied general scholarship page does not provide one universal scholarship amount for every recipient . This is because the University states that the level of award differs by region . Applicants therefore need to consult the country-specific scholarship profile to determine the amount applicable to their particular country and programme. Consequently, prospective applicants should not assume that every Global Futures Scholarship recipient will receive the same financial award. Merit-Based Nature of the Scholarship The Global Futures Scholarships are identified as partial merit-based scholarships . Applicants should therefore pay attention not only to the admission requirements for their intended programme but also to the scholarship s country-specific eligibility and selection requirements. A strong university application should clearly demonstrate the applicant s academic preparation and suitability for the chosen course. However, applicants should rely on the specific criteria provided by the University for their country when determining what information is required for the scholarship application. Study Location: Manchester, United Kingdom Successful applicants will study at The University of Manchester , located in Manchester, United Kingdom. The scholarship requires students to hold an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester . This means that the scholarship is not presented as an opportunity for online or part-time study under the general eligibility conditions provided on the scholarship page. The University of Manchester is located on Oxford Road in Manchester, UK. For international students, studying in Manchester can also provide an opportunity to experience a major UK city while undertaking university-level education in a global academic environment. How to Apply for the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 The application process begins with applying for an eligible programme at the University of Manchester. Step 1: Identify an eligible course Applicants should first research the University of Manchester s undergraduate or master s programmes and identify a course that corresponds with their academic background and future study plans. The scholarship requires the applicant to have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester . Step 2: Apply for admission to the University of Manchester The next step is to submit an application for admission to the University. Importantly, the scholarship is not presented as a standalone application that applicants can complete before obtaining university admission. The University states that applicants must hold an offer of a study place for a course beginning in September 2027. Step 3: Receive an offer of study Applicants must receive an offer for an eligible course beginning in September 2027. Once an applicant has an appropriate offer, they can proceed to the scholarship application stage if they meet the other requirements. Step 4: Complete the scholarship application The University states that eligible offer-holders will be sent an online scholarship application form by email . Applicants should therefore monitor the email address used during their university application process and carefully check messages from the University of Manchester. Step 5: Check the country-specific deadline One of the most important points for applicants is that there is no single universal deadline stated on the general Global Futures Scholarship page supplied here . Instead, the University explains that application deadlines differ according to region. Applicants should therefore check the scholarship profile for their specific country rather than relying on a deadline published for another country. APPLY HERE Deadline for the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 Deadline: Varies by country/region. The University of Manchester states that the application deadlines differ for each region and directs applicants to their country-specific scholarship profiles for the applicable deadline. This is an important consideration for prospective applicants because waiting for a general deadline could result in missing an earlier country-specific closing date. Students should check the relevant country profile as soon as possible after reviewing their eligibility and receiving their university offer. Country-Specific Scholarship Information The University provides separate scholarship information for each participating country. The country profiles linked from the Global Futures Scholarships page include: Bangladesh Botswana Canada Egypt Ghana India Indonesia Kenya Malaysia Mauritius Nigeria Pakistan Saudi Arabia Singapore South Africa Sri Lanka Taiwan Thailand Türkiye United Arab Emirates United States Vietnam Zimbabwe. These profiles are particularly important because they contain the country-specific details that determine the applicable scholarship conditions. What Applicants Should Check Before Applying Before beginning the scholarship application process, prospective students should carefully review the following: 1. Country eligibility Confirm that you are living in one of the countries listed by the University for the Global Futures Scholarships. 2. Academic level Determine whether your intended programme is at undergraduate or master s level and whether the scholarship is available for that level in your country. 3. University admission You must hold an offer from the University of Manchester for an eligible course. 4. Mode of study The general scholarship requirement specifies a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester . 5. Programme start date The course must begin in September 2027 . 6. Country-specific requirements Applicants should review the scholarship profile for their country because the award value and eligibility conditions differ by region. 7. Scholarship deadline Check the deadline associated with your country rather than relying on information from another country. 8. Scholarship application invitation Eligible offer-holders will receive information about the online scholarship application form by email. Why Applicants Should Pay Attention to the Country Profile The country profile is one of the most important parts of the Global Futures Scholarships application process. Although the general scholarship page provides an overview of the programme, the University explicitly states that award levels, eligibility criteria and application deadlines differ by region . For this reason, two applicants from different eligible countries may not necessarily have exactly the same scholarship conditions. Applicants should therefore avoid relying exclusively on general scholarship information found on third-party websites, social media pages or scholarship blogs. The country-specific information provided by the University should be used when confirming the requirements that apply to an individual application. Contact Information Applicants who need additional information about the Global Futures Scholarships can contact the University of Manchester s International Office. The scholarship page provides the following contact email: international@manchester.ac.uk The University also provides an International Team that offers support and guidance to international students. Official Scholarship Information Applicants should always verify the latest requirements, country-specific eligibility conditions, scholarship value and deadline directly with the University of Manchester before submitting an application. Visit HERE for more information about the Global Futures Scholarships 2027 at the University of Manchester. Conclusion The Global Futures Scholarships 2027 provide a significant funding opportunity for eligible international students seeking to study at the University of Manchester. For the September 2027 intake, the University is offering more than 350 partial merit-based scholarships , with the total value of awards exceeding £6 million . The opportunity is open to eligible students at undergraduate and master s level from a specified group of countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and other regions. However, eligibility is country-specific, and applicants must meet the applicable requirements for their country. A key requirement is that applicants must have an offer for a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester beginning in September 2027 . Eligible offer-holders will subsequently be invited to complete an online scholarship application. Because scholarship amounts, eligibility requirements and deadlines vary by region, prospective applicants should carefully review the country-specific scholarship information and ensure that they meet the requirements before applying. The general scholarship page does not provide one universal deadline; instead, applicants must check the deadline applicable to their country. title: UK MEET Fellowship 2026 for Journalists and Digital Content Creators in Ghana and Nigeria: Science, Technology and Emerging Media Training with Imperial College London
summary: Applications are now open for the UK–West Africa Media Excellence in Emerging Technologies (MEET) Fellowship 2026 , a professional development programme designed to strengthen the capacity of journalists and digital content creators in Ghana and Nigeria to report accurately, creatively and responsibly on science, innovation and emerging technologies. The programme is delivered by the British High Commission , working through its teams in Accra, Lagos and Abuja, in partnership with Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana . The UK MEET Fellowship responds to a growing need for media professionals who can take complicated scientific and technological subjects and translate them into accurate, engaging and accessible journalism for diverse audiences . Selected participants will take part in online preparation and an intensive six-night residential training programme in either Ghana or Nigeria. The Fellowship combines science and technology reporting with practical digital storytelling and opportunities to engage directly with researchers, policymakers, innovators and industry professionals. Participants will also develop an original story concept during the programme. On the final day of the residential training, Fellows will pitch their stories for the opportunity to receive funding to produce and publish them. A subset of participants selected through the pitch process will subsequently take part in a fully funded, week-long knowledge-exchange visit to London , including engagement with Imperial College London. The programme particularly encourages applications from women, journalists and creators outside major urban centres, applicants from underrepresented regions, and marginalized groups . The application deadline is: 22 September 2026 at 23:45 GMT Applications must be submitted through the official online form . About the UK Media Excellence in Emerging Technologies Fellowship The Media Excellence in Emerging Technologies Fellowship , commonly referred to as the MEET Fellowship or UK MEET Fellowship , is designed to strengthen media professionals ability to communicate developments in science, innovation and technology , referred to throughout the programme as SIT. Scientific and technological developments increasingly influence almost every part of public life. Artificial intelligence is changing work, education and communication. Climate and environmental risks affect communities, infrastructure and national planning. Biomedical technologies raise new possibilities and difficult ethical questions. Electronic waste and circular-economy approaches influence environmental policy, health, employment and manufacturing. Yet these subjects are often difficult to report well. Journalists and digital storytellers need to understand enough of the underlying science and technology to distinguish evidence from hype, identify credible experts, ask informed questions, explain uncertainty and communicate technical information without making it inaccessible to general audiences. The UK MEET Fellowship is built around this challenge. Rather than focusing only on conventional journalism techniques, the programme brings together science understanding, public communication, emerging technology, ethics and digital storytelling . What Is the Main Goal of the Fellowship? The programme aims to build the capacity of media professionals for excellence in: Science reporting Innovation reporting Technology reporting Digital storytelling Public communication of technical information Its central purpose is to help participants translate complex scientific and technological ideas into content that is: Accurate Accessible Engaging Relevant Responsible Useful to diverse audiences The Fellowship therefore combines subject knowledge with practical media skills. Participants are not expected simply to become experts in one technology. Instead, the programme aims to give journalists and digital creators a stronger framework for approaching unfamiliar and rapidly changing scientific subjects. Who Is Behind the UK MEET Fellowship? The programme is delivered through a partnership involving major UK institutions. British High Commission The British High Commission is a funding and delivery partner for the Fellowship. Applications from Ghana and Nigeria will be reviewed through the appropriate British High Commission teams associated with the applicant s country track. The official application information explains that participant information will be shared between Imperial College London and the relevant British High Commission teams for purposes including: Eligibility screening Shortlisting Selection Programme auditing Evaluation The initiative also connects with broader UK objectives around innovation, science partnerships and evidence-informed policymaking. Imperial College London Imperial College London participates through Imperial Global Ghana . Imperial brings substantial scientific and technological expertise to the Fellowship, creating opportunities for journalists and creators to interact with researchers rather than learning about science communication only through conventional media-training approaches. The programme s UK knowledge-exchange component also includes time at Imperial College London for selected pitch award winners. What Will Participants Learn? The Fellowship is organized around several thematic areas and five core skills. The major themes include: Artificial intelligence Climate and environmental risk Biomedical innovation Circular economy and electronic waste Other related science, innovation and technology issues Across these subjects, participants will develop five central competencies: Understanding complex scientific and technological concepts Effective science communication Navigating emerging technologies for the public good Understanding ethical considerations in science, innovation and technology reporting Engaging directly and effectively with experts These competencies are intended to be transferable across different media beats. A journalist may currently focus on health but later need to report on AI. A digital creator may focus on climate but encounter new questions around technology, agriculture or energy. The Fellowship therefore aims to strengthen the underlying skills required to approach complex evidence responsibly. Theme 1: Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence has quickly become one of the most important emerging-technology reporting areas. Journalists increasingly need to understand issues connected with: Generative AI Automation Algorithmic decision-making AI policy Data Misinformation AI and employment AI and education AI in healthcare Governance Privacy Bias Ethics Public-sector uses of AI Good AI reporting requires more than repeating claims from technology companies or presenting every new tool as revolutionary. Journalists need to ask questions such as: What can the technology actually do? What evidence supports the claims being made? Who developed it? What data does it use? Who may benefit? Who could be disadvantaged? What safeguards exist? What are the relevant regulatory debates? The Fellowship aims to equip participants with stronger tools for addressing questions of this kind. Theme 2: Climate and Environmental Risk Climate and environmental reporting often involves complicated data, scientific uncertainty and long-term trends. Potential reporting issues may include: Climate change Flooding Extreme heat Pollution Coastal risks Environmental degradation Climate adaptation Resilience Energy transitions Environmental health Journalists need to communicate these issues without either overstating evidence or minimizing genuine risks. For Ghanaian and Nigerian media professionals, these subjects can also be connected to very local questions affecting communities, livelihoods and public policy. Theme 3: Biomedical Innovation Biomedical innovation creates important opportunities for journalism at the intersection of science, health and society. Relevant subjects may include: Medical technologies Diagnostics Biotechnology Public health innovation Pharmaceutical research Genomics Health technology Digital health Clinical research Reporting on these issues requires journalists to understand not only what a new technology promises, but also what evidence exists, which stage of development it has reached and what uncertainties remain. Theme 4: Circular Economy and E-Waste The Fellowship also addresses the circular economy and electronic waste . A circular-economy approach seeks to reduce waste and extend the useful life of materials through practices such as: Reuse Repair Recycling Resource recovery More sustainable production Better product design E-waste introduces additional questions around: Environmental contamination Informal recycling Health Technology consumption International waste flows Regulation Employment Industrial policy These subjects illustrate why emerging-technology journalism increasingly requires reporters to connect science with economics, politics, health and social issues. Five Core Skills Used Throughout the Programme The programme does not treat each thematic topic as an isolated subject. Instead, five skills are applied throughout the training. 1. Understanding Complex Concepts Participants will strengthen their ability to understand scientific or technological concepts well enough to report them accurately. Journalists do not need to become scientists themselves, but they should be able to recognize: What they understand What they do not understand What questions need to be asked Which experts should be consulted Which claims require verification 2. Effective Science Communication Participants will work on communicating technical subjects clearly without sacrificing accuracy. This is especially important when producing material for audiences that may have little specialist knowledge. Effective science communication involves finding the balance between: Technical precision and public accessibility. 3. Emerging Technology for the Public Good The Fellowship also encourages participants to consider how new technologies affect society. Rather than presenting innovation as automatically positive or negative, journalists can investigate: Who gains access Who is excluded What risks emerge What policy choices are involved Whether technology addresses an actual public need 4. Ethics in Science and Technology Reporting Ethical considerations are explicitly included in the programme. These may involve questions around: Accuracy Source selection Sensationalism Privacy Conflicts of interest Representation Uncertainty Public harm Responsible use of digital tools Ethical reporting becomes particularly important where scientific issues involve health, vulnerable populations or technologies whose long-term effects remain uncertain. 5. Direct Engagement With Experts Participants will learn through direct interaction with: Researchers Policymakers Innovators Industry professionals This can help journalists build confidence in interviewing experts and develop relationships that may continue after the Fellowship. Six-Night Residential Training One of the major components of the UK MEET Fellowship is an intensive: Six-night residential training camp. The programme runs from Sunday evening through Friday evening . Participants attend the residential programme in their country of residence. Therefore: Ghana-based Fellows attend the Ghana residential programme. Nigeria-based Fellows attend the Nigeria residential programme. Applicants may only apply through the country track in which they are currently based. Programme Dates Applicants need to be available for all relevant programme components . Online Pre-Training The programme begins with: Two short online sessions plus pre-reading during the: Week of 5 October 2026 This is referred to as Phase 0 . Ghana Residential Programme The official detailed call identifies the Ghana training as the: Week of 12 October 2026 Because the residential runs from Sunday evening to Friday evening, participants should expect the residential period to begin around Sunday, 11 October , followed by the training week beginning Monday, 12 October. Nigeria Residential Programme The Nigeria training is scheduled for the: Week of 19 October 2026 With the Sunday-evening residential structure, participants should expect arrival around Sunday, 18 October , followed by the programme week beginning Monday, 19 October. UK Knowledge Exchange For selected pitch award winners, the UK visit is planned for the: Week of 30 November 2026 Applicants should note carefully that the UK knowledge-exchange visit is not automatically guaranteed to everyone who attends the residential training . It is intended for a selected subset of participants associated with the story-pitch award stage. Digital Skills Development An important part of the Fellowship is hands-on digital storytelling. Training includes areas such as: Platform strategy Short-form video Data storytelling Visual design These skills reflect the rapidly changing ways audiences consume journalism. Media professionals increasingly need to understand how the same story may need to be adapted for: News websites Social media Short-form video Visual platforms Mobile audiences Data-led storytelling formats The Fellowship therefore recognizes that strong science communication depends not only on the accuracy of information but also on how that information is presented. Networking Opportunities Participants will have structured opportunities to engage with: Leading researchers Policymakers Innovators Industry professionals Fellow journalists Digital content creators These relationships can be particularly valuable for science and technology journalists because reliable reporting often depends on access to credible specialist sources. A journalist who develops a network of researchers during the Fellowship may later be better positioned to obtain: Expert interpretation Background briefings Technical clarification Alternative perspectives Leads for future stories Pitch for Story Funding The Fellowship moves beyond classroom-style training by asking participants to develop an original journalism story concept. On the final day of the residential programme , participants will pitch their developed idea for a chance to receive an award to: Produce and publish the story. This creates a direct bridge between training and real media output. The public call does not state the monetary value of the pitch award. Therefore, applicants should not assume or advertise a specific amount unless organizers subsequently provide one. What Could Make a Strong Story Pitch? Although the programme does not prescribe one formula for a successful pitch, a promising story concept would likely benefit from having: A clear science, innovation or technology connection Strong relevance to the public A clearly identifiable audience Evidence of a genuine problem or question Potential access to credible experts Original reporting potential Clear public-interest value An appropriate digital storytelling approach Candidates may benefit from thinking about possible story ideas even before entering the programme. Fully Funded UK Knowledge-Exchange Visit A selected subset of participants will have the opportunity to join a: Fully funded, week-long knowledge-exchange visit to London. The programme includes time at Imperial College London . The visit is scheduled for the week of: 30 November 2026 The detailed eligibility guidance also requires applicants to hold, or be capable of obtaining in time, a valid international passport because some participants may be selected for this international component. Again, the distinction is important: Residential Fellowship participation does not automatically guarantee selection for the UK visit. Minimum Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all seven minimum eligibility requirements . The organizers explicitly state that applicants who do not meet every minimum requirement will not be able to submit a complete application. 1. Applicants Must Be at Least 18 Applicants must be: 18 years old or above. There is no maximum age stated in the official call. 2. Applicants Must Be Based in Ghana or Nigeria Applicants must currently be based in: Ghana, or Nigeria Candidates must apply through the country track where they are currently based. Applicants cannot choose another country s track simply because its residential dates are more convenient. 3. Applicants Must Be Journalists or Eligible Digital Content Creators Applicants must currently work as one of the following: Journalists Working in: Print media Broadcast media Online media or: Social Media Content Creators Creators must have an: Active and publicly viewable presence on at least one relevant platform. The official call specifically names: TikTok Instagram YouTube X Facebook For creators, that public presence must feature content relevant to science, innovation or technology. This is an important expansion beyond conventional newsroom journalism. The Fellowship is therefore open not only to journalists employed by traditional media organizations, but also to qualifying digital-first creators. 4. Applicants Need at Least Five Recent SIT Content Pieces Applicants must have produced at least: Five original pieces of content on science, innovation or technology-related themes within the: Previous 12 months. Applicants must have links available to share. Eligible subject matter can include areas such as: Climate Health Technology Agriculture Energy Related science and innovation themes This requirement demonstrates that the programme is looking for applicants who already have some practical engagement with relevant subjects. It is not simply an introductory programme for someone who has never produced any science- or technology-related content. 5. Full Attendance Is Mandatory Applicants must be able to participate in: Phase 0 online preparation Full in-country residential programme The official call clearly states: Partial attendance is not possible. This means applicants should compare the programme schedule carefully against: Work obligations Travel Other professional commitments Personal responsibilities before submitting an application. 6. International Passport Requirement Applicants must either: Already hold a valid international passport, or Be capable of obtaining one in time This is necessary because selected participants may travel to the United Kingdom for the knowledge-exchange component. Applicants without a passport at the application stage are not necessarily automatically excluded, provided they are genuinely able to obtain one within the required timeframe. 7. Professional English Ability Applicants must be comfortable: Working and communicating professionally in English. The programme does not state that candidates need to submit an IELTS, TOEFL or other formal English-language certificate. The requirement concerns functional professional communication. Selection Criteria and Scoring Candidates who satisfy all seven eligibility conditions move to competitive evaluation. The official call provides a clear weighted selection framework. Relevance to SIT Themes – 35% This is the largest component of the assessment. Applicants will be evaluated on demonstrated experience reporting or creating content on: Science Innovation Technology Related subjects This means applicants should choose previous work examples strategically. Quality of Previous Work – 30% Nearly one-third of the evaluation is based on the quality of the applicant s previous journalism or digital content. Applicants will provide links to their work. Reviewers can therefore examine actual evidence of the candidate s: Reporting Storytelling Accuracy Audience communication Digital media skills Potential for Impact – 25% Applicants need to explain clearly how participating in UK MEET could: Improve their work Expand their reach Strengthen their journalism Help communicate science more effectively The programme will also consider alignment with broader FCDO goals, including: Fostering innovation Strengthening UK–Ghana partnerships Strengthening UK–Nigeria partnerships Promoting evidence-based policymaking Applicants should therefore think beyond personal career development and explain how the programme could improve their wider professional impact. Collaboration Readiness – 5% Applicants may receive additional credit for demonstrating readiness to collaborate. The call particularly mentions applicants who have already identified: Researchers Research areas Research topics whose work they would like to amplify. This accounts for 5% of the assessment . Diversity and Inclusion – 5% The final weighted component considers: Gender balance Regional representation Participation outside major urban centres Inclusion of underrepresented voices The programme aims for: At least 40% women in its cohorts. This does not mean that only women are eligible. It means gender representation forms part of the cohort-building process. Selection Criteria at a Glance Criterion Weight Relevance to science, innovation and technology themes 35% Quality of previous work 30% Potential for impact 25% Collaboration readiness 5% Diversity and inclusion 5% Applicants can use this weighting strategically. Because 65% of the score comes from thematic relevance and previous work quality , choosing strong published work examples is likely to be particularly important. Women Are Strongly Encouraged to Apply Women applicants are explicitly encouraged. The programme targets at least: 40% female representation within its cohorts. This is an encouragement and selection consideration rather than a women-only eligibility condition. Applicants of other genders remain eligible if they satisfy the programme requirements. Applicants Outside Major Cities Are Encouraged The selection framework specifically values: Regional representation, including locations outside major urban centres. This is significant for journalists who might assume that applicants in Accra, Lagos or Abuja automatically have an advantage. Media professionals based elsewhere in Ghana or Nigeria are expressly encouraged to participate. Marginalized and Underrepresented Applicants The programme also strongly encourages applications from: Marginalized groups Underrepresented voices Underrepresented regions The call does not restrict eligibility to any one racial, ethnic or social group. Instead, diversity is treated as part of building a broader and more representative cohort. How to Apply Applicants must submit the official online application form. Application form: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ugjTfMLCWQ The application begins with an eligibility screening process. Applicants should therefore verify that they meet all seven minimum requirements before beginning. The organizers also provide a detailed Call for Applications explaining: Programme objectives Benefits Dates Eligibility Selection criteria Application requirements Information Provided Through the Application The application process begins with basic information such as: First name Last name Email address Gender How the applicant heard about the programme Country track The application then determines eligibility before allowing applicants to proceed with the full submission. Because prior science and technology work forms a major part of selection, candidates should prepare links to at least five qualifying pieces of original work produced within the previous 12 months. Data and Privacy Imperial College London states that information collected through the application form will be used to: Assess applications Screen eligibility Shortlist candidates Make selection decisions Conduct programme auditing Conduct programme evaluation Application information will also be accessible to the relevant British High Commission teams in accordance with the applicant s country track. Candidates should review the privacy information linked in the application before submission. How to Prepare a Competitive Application 1. Choose Your Five Strongest Work Samples Carefully Do not simply submit the first five SIT-related pieces you can find. Because previous work quality and thematic relevance together represent 65% of the selection weighting , choose examples that demonstrate: Strong reporting Originality Public relevance Clear explanation Good sourcing Appropriate use of evidence 2. Show Breadth or Depth in SIT Reporting If you have reported repeatedly on one topic, demonstrate clear subject knowledge. If your work covers multiple themes, explain how the Fellowship would help you build a more coherent science and technology reporting practice. 3. Explain Your Potential Impact Specifically Avoid generic statements such as: “I want to improve my journalism skills.” Instead, explain what will change. For example: Will you establish a regular technology column? Produce more evidence-based climate journalism? Expand science reporting in your regional newsroom? Build short-form video explainers? Train colleagues? Reach audiences currently underserved by science journalism? Concrete plans make potential impact easier to understand. 4. Identify Researchers or Research Topics Because collaboration readiness is assessed, applicants may strengthen their submission by identifying: Researchers whose work interests them Universities or laboratories Emerging technology questions Research fields deserving wider media coverage This shows that the applicant is already thinking about journalism-research collaboration. 5. Think About Your Story Pitch in Advance You do not need to arrive with a finished story. However, having a promising direction can help you take fuller advantage of the residential programme. Consider: What emerging-technology issue affects your audience? Who is missing from current coverage? Where is there a gap between research and public understanding? What question deserves original reporting? 6. Check Your Passport Since pitch winners may travel to London soon after the residential training, passport preparation should not be left until the last minute. The UK exchange is scheduled for the week of 30 November 2026 , only several weeks after the Ghana and Nigeria residential programmes. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 22 September 2026 at 23:45 GMT The call identifies GMT/Accra time for the deadline. Applicants should submit early enough to avoid technical difficulties close to closing time. six-night residential structure beginning Sunday evening Nigeria residential: Week beginning 19 October 2026, with the six-night residential structure beginning Sunday evening UK knowledge exchange for selected pitch award winners: Week of 30 November 2026 Key Information at a Glance Programme: UK–West Africa Media Excellence in Emerging Technologies Fellowship 2026 Short name: UK MEET Fellowship / MEET Fellowship Partners: British High Commission and Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana Eligible countries: Ghana and Nigeria Target participants: Journalists and qualifying digital/social media content creators Minimum age: 18 Relevant media: Print, broadcast, online journalism and eligible digital content platforms Required previous work: At least five original science, innovation or technology-related pieces during the previous 12 months Training: Six-night residential programme plus online pre-training Digital skills: Platform strategy, short-form video, data storytelling and visual design Professional engagement: Researchers, policymakers, innovators and industry professionals Story opportunity: Pitch for an award to produce and publish an original story UK component: Fully funded, week-long London knowledge exchange for selected participants/pitch award winners English: Professional working and communication ability required Passport: Valid passport or ability to obtain one in time required Deadline: 22 September 2026 at 23:45 GMT Application: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ugjTfMLCWQ Questions: imperialglobalghana@imperial.ac.uk Conclusion The UK Media Excellence in Emerging Technologies Fellowship 2026 offers journalists and digital content creators in Ghana and Nigeria an intensive opportunity to strengthen the quality of science, innovation and technology reporting in West Africa. The programme goes considerably beyond a short journalism workshop. Participants will complete online preparation, join a six-night residential training programme, build practical skills in digital storytelling and engage directly with researchers, policymakers, innovators and industry professionals. Training will address some of the most consequential emerging issues facing contemporary media, including artificial intelligence, climate and environmental risk, biomedical innovation, circular economy and electronic waste . At the same time, participants will develop transferable skills in interpreting complexity, communicating science, considering ethical questions and reporting emerging technologies in the public interest. The programme also creates a practical pathway from learning to publication. Fellows will develop and pitch original stories, with selected pitches receiving an award to support production and publication. Selected participants will subsequently join a fully funded, week-long UK knowledge-exchange visit , including engagement at Imperial College London. Eligibility is more specific than simply being a journalist in Ghana or Nigeria. Applicants must be at least 18, be currently based in one of the two countries, work as an eligible journalist or digital creator, have produced at least five original SIT-related pieces within the previous 12 months, commit to the entire training schedule, be able to obtain an international passport and work professionally in English. Selection is competitive. Relevance to science, innovation and technology accounts for 35% of the assessment, quality of previous work for 30%, potential impact for 25%, collaboration readiness for 5%, and diversity and inclusion for 5%. Women, applicants from underrepresented parts of Ghana and Nigeria, people outside major media centres and marginalized groups are particularly encouraged to apply.
