title: Google for Startups Immersion EMEA 2026: Apply for the Google x Antler Program for High-Growth Startups
summary: Applications are now open for the Google for Startups Immersion – EMEA 2026 , an intensive startup development program created for ambitious founders across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) who are already building companies with live products and demonstrated traction. Powered by Google for Startups and Antler , the 2026 Immersion program combines Google s technical and product expertise with Antler s experience in venture building, startup strategy and investment. Unlike an introductory entrepreneurship course aimed at people who only have a business idea, Google for Startups Immersion EMEA 2026 is targeted at founders who have already moved into execution. Participating startups are expected to have products in the market and evidence of traction. The program will begin with a series of virtual sessions in October 2026. Following the online phase, 25 startups will be invited to participate in an exclusive in-person Immersion experience in London on December 1, 2026 , where selected founders will gain access to Google engineers, Antler mentors, technical support and investor networking opportunities. The application deadline is October 13, 2026 . About Google for Startups Immersion EMEA 2026 Google for Startups Immersion EMEA is designed to help high-potential startup founders address both the technical and commercial challenges involved in scaling a technology company . The initiative combines two complementary areas of expertise. Google brings its technology ecosystem, engineers, product expertise and experience supporting technology companies, while Antler contributes venture-building knowledge, investment perspectives, mentorship and expertise in areas such as fundraising, go-to-market strategy and business economics. The result is a program that goes beyond generic startup education. Participants will have opportunities to examine both the technology behind their businesses and the commercial foundations required to build sustainable, scalable companies. The program is therefore particularly relevant for startup leadership teams seeking to improve their technology architecture, AI capabilities, business strategy, unit economics, fundraising readiness and overall approach to scaling. How the Google for Startups Immersion Program Works The 2026 program is structured around two main phases . Phase One: Virtual Immersion Sessions The first phase will take place virtually from October 22 to October 28, 2026 . During this stage, participating startups will have access to four online sessions covering technical and business topics. Importantly, the program uses dedicated or dual tracks designed to address the different responsibilities of startup founders and technical leaders. The sessions are expected to cover areas including: Google s AI and development technologies; Google Antigravity; Gemini Enterprise; AI Studio; AI investing; Venture-capital mathematics and strategy; Unit economics; Building defensible businesses; and Technical and commercial considerations associated with scaling a startup. The structure reflects the reality that scaling a technology startup requires more than building a technically impressive product. Founders also need to understand whether the business model is sustainable, whether customer acquisition and pricing strategies make sense, how the company can defend its market position and how investors may evaluate its economics. At the same time, CTOs and technical leaders need to ensure that the underlying technology can support growth. The virtual phase therefore brings these dimensions together. Phase Two: In-Person Immersion in London Following the online phase, 25 startups will be selected and invited to participate in an exclusive in-person Immersion program in London on December 1, 2026 . The London phase takes the program deeper into startup-specific technical and business challenges. Selected companies can expect opportunities for direct interaction with Google engineers and Antler mentors. The in-person program is reported to include: Technical architecture sessions with Google engineers; Live technical problem-solving and “bug squashing”; One-on-one Antler mentorship; Go-to-market strategy discussions; Pricing guidance; Fundraising mentorship; Business-model and scaling discussions; and A private founder and investor mixer. This second phase is therefore considerably more targeted than a conventional startup conference. Rather than simply listening to presentations, selected founders will have opportunities to engage directly with experts around the challenges facing their companies. Technical Support from Google Technology is one of the core pillars of the Immersion program. For founders building AI-enabled or technology-intensive products, scaling can introduce substantial challenges involving infrastructure, product architecture, reliability, integrations and development workflows. The program gives participating companies exposure to Google s technical expertise and technology ecosystem. The virtual curriculum includes technologies such as Google Antigravity and Gemini Enterprise , while the London stage provides selected startups with more direct technical interaction with Google engineers. For startups already operating live products, this type of engagement can be particularly relevant because technical challenges tend to become more complex as usage increases. Business and Venture Support from Antler The second major component of the program comes from Antler. Antler is a global early-stage venture capital firm and startup ecosystem participant that works with founders in multiple markets. Through the Immersion program, Antler contributes expertise on the commercial and investment side of building a high-growth startup. The program covers topics including: Venture capital strategy; Startup economics; Unit economics; Defensibility; Go-to-market strategy; Pricing; and Fundraising. For the companies selected for London, this support becomes more personalized through one-on-one mentorship with Antler . Founder and CTO Tracks One notable feature of the virtual stage is the use of separate or dual learning tracks. Startup founders and CTOs frequently face different but interconnected challenges. A founder or CEO may spend substantial time considering customer acquisition, market positioning, financing, pricing, hiring and investor relationships. A CTO or technical co-founder may be focused more heavily on architecture, infrastructure, engineering processes, AI implementation, security, product performance and technical scalability. Google for Startups Immersion addresses both sides rather than treating every member of a startup s leadership team as having identical development needs. This approach can help startup leadership teams align technology decisions with commercial objectives. Who Should Apply? The program is specifically aimed at ambitious founders across the EMEA region who already have a live product and demonstrated traction . EMEA refers to: Europe, the Middle East and Africa. This means the program is not primarily targeted at aspiring entrepreneurs who are still deciding what company to create. Applicants should already be building and operating a startup. Current descriptions of the program emphasize two important characteristics: A live product: The startup should have moved beyond the purely conceptual stage and have a product in the market. Traction: Applicants should be able to demonstrate evidence that the company has progressed beyond simply developing an idea. What Does “Traction” Mean for Startup Applicants? The official program materials emphasize demonstrated traction, although the publicly available information does not establish one universal numerical threshold that every applicant must meet. In a startup context, traction can generally refer to evidence that a company is gaining meaningful market validation. Depending on the business model, evidence may include customers, users, revenue, recurring usage, commercial partnerships, growth or other indicators showing genuine adoption. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting verifiable indicators appropriate to their own business model rather than assuming that every startup will be assessed using an identical metric. Who Is This Program Best Suited For? The program is particularly relevant to founders who have already completed the earliest stages of startup formation and are now confronting questions associated with growth. This could include companies seeking to: Improve their technology architecture; Scale an existing product; Integrate or expand AI capabilities; Strengthen unit economics; Develop stronger go-to-market strategies; Refine pricing; Prepare for fundraising; Improve their understanding of venture capital; Strengthen their competitive defensibility; or Connect with other founders, mentors and investors. Because the program requires a live product and traction, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate that their startup has already progressed beyond the idea stage. Exposure to Other EMEA Founders Another component of the Immersion experience is access to other startup founders from across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. This creates an environment in which participants can exchange experiences with companies operating in different markets and sectors. Building a startup in EMEA can involve very different market conditions depending on the founder s location. European companies may face one regulatory, investment and customer environment, while startups operating in Africa or the Middle East may encounter different infrastructure, financing and market-access dynamics. Bringing founders from these regions into the same program creates opportunities for cross-market learning and potentially future collaboration. Access to Potential Investors The London phase is also expected to provide selected startups with investor exposure. A private founder and investor mixer is among the reported elements of the in-person Immersion. This gives selected founders an additional networking opportunity alongside the program s technical and business-development activities. Applicants should nevertheless distinguish between access to investor networking and guaranteed investment. The available program information does not mean that admission automatically results in investment or funding. Is Google for Startups Immersion a Funding Program? The central offering described in the available 2026 program information is technical and business support, mentorship, expert access and networking , rather than a guaranteed cash award. Accordingly, applicants should not interpret participation as an automatic Google or Antler investment. The value proposition instead centers on access to expertise, startup development resources, technical guidance, venture mentorship and connections. Key Program Dates Applicants should take careful note of the 2026 timeline: Application deadline: October 13, 2026 Virtual program: October 22–28, 2026 Number of virtual sessions: Four Startups invited to the in-person phase: Up to 25 London Immersion: December 1, 2026 The application window is therefore followed relatively quickly by the virtual program, so founders should consider their availability for the October sessions before applying. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Google for Startups Immersion – EMEA 2026 is: October 13, 2026 Founders interested in participating should submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. How to Apply Applications are being managed through Google s official event portal. Founders should first review the eligibility criteria and program structure and then complete the requested application information accurately. When preparing an application, startup teams should be ready to clearly communicate: What their company does; The problem the startup is solving; Who uses or purchases the product; Evidence that the product is already live; Evidence of market traction; The startup s growth trajectory; Key technical or commercial challenges; The strength and composition of the founding team; and Why participating in the Immersion program would be relevant to the company s current stage. Where quantitative information is requested, founders should provide accurate and supportable information rather than overstating traction. Official Application Page Applications and official program information are available through Google s event portal: Apply for Google for Startups Immersion – EMEA 2026 Why the Two-Phase Structure Matters The program s two-stage structure allows the Immersion experience to move from broad learning toward more concentrated company-specific support. During the first phase, participating founders can develop their understanding of relevant Google technologies and key venture-building concepts. The second phase then narrows participation to 25 startups for a more intensive in-person experience. For selected companies, this creates an opportunity to move from general learning toward direct technical discussions, individual mentorship and networking. Google Technology Meets Antler s Venture-Building Expertise The defining characteristic of the 2026 Immersion is the combination of Google s technology expertise and Antler s venture perspective. High-growth technology startups must solve both technical and commercial problems. A technically sophisticated product does not automatically produce a sustainable business. Conversely, a strong commercial strategy cannot compensate indefinitely for technology that cannot scale. The Immersion program addresses these interconnected dimensions by exposing founders to technical specialists as well as business and investment expertise. This makes the program especially relevant for founders reaching the point where product, technology, economics and growth strategy must work together. Conclusion The Google for Startups Immersion – EMEA 2026, powered by Antler , provides founders across Europe, the Middle East and Africa with an opportunity to strengthen both the technical and commercial foundations of their startups. Designed specifically for companies with live products and demonstrated traction , the program begins with four virtual sessions from October 22–28, 2026 , covering Google technologies and essential venture-building topics. The experience can then progress further for 25 selected startups , which will be invited to an in-person Immersion in London on December 1, 2026 . The London program is expected to provide deeper access to Google engineers, one-on-one Antler mentorship, technical problem-solving, guidance around go-to-market strategy, pricing and fundraising, and opportunities to connect with founders and potential investors. Founders across the EMEA region who already have products in market and can demonstrate traction should review the official requirements and submit their applications by October 13, 2026 .
